recommendation.summary: S6 transactional patch set of 4 function(s) (interface-level (signature/added/removed functions) with call-graph closure change).
justification: no state-schema, dependency, toolchain, goroutine-structure or long-running-code change
every member of the patch set is an ordinary non-generic function or method, so each can be redirected through its slot, and the whole set is published in one atomic PatchSet store
signature changes and removals were closed over their callers; new functions and types live in the patch plugin
alternatives: S2 Go plugin swap of the affected handler (same toolchain; old code leaks)
S1 epoch swap if v2 is compiled in alongside v1 (pre-staged release)
S5 FD-passing handoff (identity state transfer) or rolling update as fallback
risks: changed functions are small enough to be inlined; with S6 slot trampolines the call still dispatches through the slot, but raw binary patching (internal/livepatch) must also patch the inlining callers: github.com/go-chi/chi/v5/middleware.Recoverer
no patched function has a context.Context parameter: S6 gives per-call (not per-request) consistency, so one request may mix old and new versions of the 4 functions

patch_set.reason: body changed; calls prettyStack.parse whose signature changed
